newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Weak Irish bonds slide further on strong US data.
newsitem.headline: Weak Irish bonds slide further on strong US data.

text.p: Irish bonds continued to weaken in patchy Tuesday afternoon trade as stronger-than-expected U.S. housing starts data dented fragile sentiment further, dealers said.
U.S. housing starts were up 9.2 percent in November, the biggest rise since July 1995.

"Trade in European markets overall has been fairly thin so a move back in U.S. bonds is enough to weaken Europe further," one dealer said, adding that the German benchmark Bund, which had been trading above par earlier, slipped back to 99.92 in the afternoon session.
The dealer said the Irish 10-year bond shed about 40 pence on best levels and the five-year bond was down about 35 pence.
Dealers said despite strong data it was unlikely the Fed's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meeting, which started today, would lead to a change in U.S. interest rates.
In a Reuters poll, twenty-two economists surveyed on Friday unanimously agreed the FOMC would leave leave the key federal funds rates at 5.25 percent.

"I think it is very unlikely that the FOMC meeting will result in a rate change, they would want see further evidence of strength before they would move," a dealer said. "They (the Fed) seem to be pretty happy with the way things have gone so far."
By 1530 GMT, the Irish 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had eased a quarter point to 101.40 to yield 6.15 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 slipped 35 pence to 108.50 to yield 6.76 percent.
